chunks: And that which was narrated - Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from them (peace be upon them) who said:
"When you break your fast from Ramadan, do not fast voluntarily after the breaking of fast except after three days have passed."

The meaning in it is that there is not in the fasting of these days the virtue and blessing thereof as there is in other days, although fasting them is permissible according to what the report contained of choice.
As for the fasting of the Day of Arafah, encouragement has come regarding it according to what the report contained, and dislike has also come regarding it.
As for what came regarding encouragement, it is what was narrated:

key_terms.صِيَامُ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ: Fasting of the Day of Arafah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on voluntary fasting in the three days immediately following Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the ruling on voluntary fasting in the days immediately following Ramadan, distinguishing between general permissibility and the lack of specific virtue (*fadl*) in those days compared to others. It contrasts this with the Day of Arafah, where scholarly discourse balances encouragement (*tarhib*) with specific contexts of dislike (*karahiya*), likely referring to the Imam’s practice or particular conditions. The text serves to refine the understanding of *sunnah* fasting periods by emphasizing the qualitative difference in spiritual reward between ordinary days and those with distinct prophetic or imamic precedents.
